topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview of cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the learning outcomes, historical context, and conceptual framework for studying the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Deregulated growth signaling pathways in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in receptor tyrosine kinase and Wnt/beta-catenin pathways drive sustained proliferation and growth factor independence.

topics.label: Blockade of terminal cell differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells arrest normal maturation pathways in both hematopoietic lineages and the intestinal epithelium.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis via p53 and Bcl-2 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how mutations disrupting p53 and Bcl-2 family interactions enable cancer cells to resist programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, telomere biology, and senescence bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanisms of telomere shortening, senescence barriers, and telomerase reactivation that confer unlimited proliferative potential.

topics.label: Transition to complex hallmarks and cancer metabolic reprogramming
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics bridge from cell-autonomous growth to complex cancer hallmarks, detailing the Warburg effect, global metabolic changes, and oncometabolites.

topics.label: Angiogenic switch and tumor vascularization
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how tumors overcome diffusion limits by activating endothelial growth and vessel formation.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and biology of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how cancer cells invade, circulate, overcome metastatic inefficiency, and colonize distant tissues.

topics.label: Summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with a recap of hallmark integration and final housekeeping comments.
